definitions.explanation: The time when the sun goes below the horizon in the evening. Also refers to the phenomenon itself.

examples.japanese: {日|ひ}の{入|い}りが{早|はや}くなった。
{今日|きょう}の{日|ひ}の{入|い}りは{六時半|ろくじはん}ごろだ。
{海|うみ}に{沈|しず}む{美|うつく}しい{日|ひ}の{入|い}りを{見|み}ながら、{写真|しゃしん}を{撮|と}った。
examples.english: I took photos while watching the beautiful sunset sinking into the sea.

notes:
Literally 'the sun's entering' ({日|ひ} sun + の possessive + {入|い}り entering). Describes the sun setting below the horizon.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {日|ひ}の{入|い}りの{時刻|じこく}: sunset time
- {日|ひ}の{入|い}りが{早|はや}い: sunset is early
- {日|ひ}の{入|い}りが{遅|おそ}い: sunset is late
- {日|ひ}の{入|い}りを{見|み}る: to watch the sunset

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {夕日|ゆうひ}: the evening sun, setting sun — refers more to the visual appearance of the sun as it sets, often with poetic or aesthetic overtones
- {日没|にちぼつ}: sunset — a more formal, technical term used in weather reports and astronomy
- {日|ひ}の{出|で}: sunrise — the counterpart, referring to the sun rising in the morning

SEASONAL NOTE:
Sunset times vary significantly by season in Japan. In winter, sunset can be as early as 4:30 PM, while in summer it can be past 7:00 PM. Weather forecasts and news commonly report {日|ひ}の{出|で} and {日|ひ}の{入|い}り times.
